run.question:
Alertmanager alert RequestErrorRate (severity warning) is firing for service otel-demo/frontend-proxy since 2026-11-15T09:44:53Z.
Investigate why this alert is firing.

report.summary: The RequestErrorRate alert for otel-demo/frontend-proxy is firing on real HTTP 504 responses recorded on frontend-proxy's own ingress spans (53.7413 STATUS_CODE_ERROR spans in the 13 minutes ending 2026-11-15T09:57:41Z, about 1.07% of ingress spans). Every sampled 504 trace shows the proxy's upstream egress span to the frontend failing at ~15.000s with http.status_code=0 while the frontend's own 'GET /api/recommendations' span completes at ~15.077s with HTTP 200, so the proxy's ~15s timeout elapses just before the frontend answers. Inside that trace the time is spent on the frontend's client span grpc.oteldemo.RecommendationService/ListRecommendations (~15.074s), while product-catalog server spans are 38-2053us. The recommendation workload is the breaking dependency: after ~09:45 its span duration histogram counts fall to 0 for every bucket in the 10 minutes ending 09:57:41Z and its calls counter drops to 0, while its container CPU sat pinned at its 100m limit (0.012 -> ~0.10 cores at 09:42-09:43Z) and CFS throttling rose from ~4-6% to 69-98%; it was still receiving requests in its logs until 09:49:57.85Z. The pod is healthy at Kubernetes level (Running, Ready, restartCount 0, empty lastState, no rollout), so the failure is CPU starvation of the recommendation container rather than a crash. What drove recommendation's CPU consumption up is not established by the available evidence.

claims.text: frontend-proxy reports error spans only on operation 'ingress': 53.7413 STATUS_CODE_ERROR spans versus 4954.74 STATUS_CODE_UNSET ingress spans in the 13 minutes ending 2026-11-15T09:57:41Z (about 1.07% of ingress spans); its 'router frontend egress' spans carried 0 STATUS_CODE_ERROR in the same window.

The sampled error spans of frontend-proxy's 'ingress' operation are all HTTP 504 with otel.status_code=ERROR and duration ~15.000s, each with a child 'router frontend egress' span of ~15.000s carrying error="true" and http.status_code="0", e.g. trace 40fc89a0cadcbbb31ce5939d98b85f7e: ingress 15,001,799us and 504, egress 15,001,396us.

In trace 40fc89a0cadcbbb31ce5939d98b85f7e the frontend's own span 'GET /api/recommendations' lasts 15,077,075us and returns http.status_code=200, its internal span 'executing api route (pages) /api/recommendations' 15,076,498us, and its client span 'grpc.oteldemo.RecommendationService/ListRecommendations' 15,074,102us with rpc.grpc.status_code=0; product-catalog server spans in the same trace are 38-2053us and no recommendation-service span appears in it.

In the 13 minutes ending 09:57:41Z exactly 101.16 frontend spans exceeded 10,000ms and they are confined to four span names on one path: 'GET', 'GET /api/recommendations', 'executing api route (pages) /api/recommendations' and 'grpc.oteldemo.RecommendationService/ListRecommendations'; no other frontend operation exceeded 10s.

Comparable baseline: over the 59 minutes ending 09:43:53Z, the same calculation returned 0 for all 24 frontend operations, including 'GET /api/recommendations' and 'grpc.oteldemo.RecommendationService/ListRecommendations', so the >10s behaviour began inside the incident rather than before it.

frontend-proxy 504s per one-minute bucket were 0 through 09:43:00, then 2 at 09:44:00, 12 at 09:45:00, 8 at 09:46:00, 30 at 09:47:00, 28 at 09:48:00, 2 at 09:49:00, 20 at 09:50:00, 6 at 09:51:00, 8 at 09:52:00 and 0 at 09:53:00; the 2-minute ingress error ratio peaked at 2.55% at 09:48:00 and was 0 by 09:54:40.

The recommendation service stopped completing spans: its ListRecommendations duration histogram counts were 0 in every bucket including le="+Inf" for 09:47:41-09:57:41Z, and its calls counter for '/oteldemo.RecommendationService/ListRecommendations', '/oteldemo.ProductCatalogService/ListProducts' and 'get_product_list' fell from ~220-310 spans per 5m to 0 in the 5m window ending 09:47:53Z.

Before the cut-off the recommendation service was fast: in the 10 minutes ending 09:45:00Z it recorded 447.37 ListRecommendations spans, of which 392.63 were <=10ms and only 5 were above 50ms (le=50.0).

The recommendation container's CPU usage (1m rate, container="recommendation") was ~0.012 cores from 09:36:00 to 09:41:00, rose to 0.0987 at 09:43:00 and stayed at ~0.084-0.096 cores through 09:52:00 against its declared 100m CPU limit, then fell to 0.040 at 09:53:00.

CFS throttling for the recommendation container rose from 4.3-6.0% at the 5m points 09:19:53-09:39:53Z to 69.4% at 09:44:53Z, 96.5% at 09:49:53Z and 97.8% at 09:54:53Z, while every other otel-demo container's throttling ratio stayed at its previous level (e.g. frontend 20-28%, product-catalog 16-23%, frontend-proxy 3-6%, ad 4-18%).

The recommendation workload is healthy at Kubernetes level: Deployment recommendation is 1/1 available (image ghcr.io/open-telemetry/demo:2.1.3-recommendation, request cpu 30m and limit 100m, memory 80Mi/160Mi), and pod recommendation-5f45f75855-htttv is Phase Running, Ready=True, restartCount 0, lastState empty, container started 09:03:32Z, owned by ReplicaSet recommendation-5f45f75855 which is owned by Deployment recommendation and was created 09:03:30Z.

The recommendation container's memory working set grew from 84.4MB to 108.9MB between 09:19:53Z and 09:54:53Z against a 160Mi limit; it did not reach the limit and the container has no termination record, so no OOM kill is shown.

The recommendation pod's logs in 09:35:00-09:57:41Z contain 749 lines; the newest 120 lines are all normal 'Receive ListRecommendations for product ids:...' receipts and the newest log line of the pod is 09:49:57.85Z, after which no further output exists in the window.

In the 13 minutes ending 09:57:41Z the only error spans in the metric were frontend-proxy 'ingress' (53.7413) plus ~1.05 flagd.evaluation.v1.Service/EventStream spans each on ad and fraud-detection, and the frontend service recorded 0 STATUS_CODE_ERROR spans throughout the hour.

product-catalog did not degrade: its span throughput stayed at ~2700-3270 spans per 5m across the incident window, its CFS throttling ratio stayed 16-23%, and its server spans in the 09:48 trace on the recommendation path were 38-2053us.

Rejected: that recommendation crashed, was OOM-killed, evicted or rolled out during the incident. The pod is Running and Ready with restartCount 0 and an empty lastState, its ReplicaSet was created at 09:03:30Z and stayed at 1 ready replica, and no recommendation or frontend events were returned for the window.

Rejected: that frontend or frontend-proxy itself ran out of CPU or that the proxy failed to route. frontend-proxy throttling stayed 2.9-4.7% and frontend 20-28%, unchanged from baseline, while recommendation alone rose to ~97%, and the proxy marks the ingress span 504 only after its egress span to the frontend reaches ~15.000s.

Primary causal chain supported by the evidence: the recommendation container's CPU demand rose to its 100m limit (usage 0.012 -> ~0.10 cores at 09:42-09:43Z, ~97% CFS throttling from 09:44Z), starving the process so that ListRecommendations no longer returned within the proxy's ~15s upstream timeout; the frontend therefore held 'GET /api/recommendations' for ~15.07s, frontend-proxy's egress call expired at ~15.000s and it returned 504, producing the RequestErrorRate condition on frontend-proxy.

Second, unresolved candidate: the increase in recommendation's CPU cost per request was not driven by more traffic, since its span rate stayed at ~220-310 per 5m before and during the spike and product-catalog answers stayed sub-millisecond, so an internal CPU-consuming condition in the recommendation process (for example a busy loop, GC or thread growth, or work triggered by flag evaluation) remains a plausible trigger that the available metrics and logs cannot identify.

Treat the recommendation Deployment's 100m CPU limit as the likely binding constraint for this path: capture a CPU profile or thread dump of the recommendation container while it is saturated, then either raise its CPU limit or add headroom or autoscaling, and re-test ListRecommendations latency against the frontend-proxy egress timeout.

Verify the frontend-proxy route timeout against the observed ~15.000s egress expiry and the frontend's ~15.07s response, because the two are close enough that the proxy aborts just before the frontend replies; validate the change with a test of the /api/recommendations route.

gaps: The RequestErrorRate alerting rule is not loaded in this Prometheus: list_prometheus_rules with rule_name=RequestErrorRate returned status no_data, so the alert expression and its reported current value 0.06666666666666667 could not be verified; the closest span-metric ratios observed were ~1.07% over 13m and a 2.55% peak over 2m.

The trigger of the recommendation container's CPU consumption increase (0.012 -> ~0.10 cores at ~09:42-09:43Z) is not identified: no CPU profile, process-level metric, deployment/config change or flag change is available, and the change_history integration is not offered in this Run.

frontend-proxy configuration is not readable: the otel-demo namespace holds only 4 ConfigMaps and none matches frontend-proxy/envoy/proxy (that query returned status no_data), so the ~15s upstream timeout is inferred from span durations and not verified against configuration.

The error-keyword log query over the recommendation pod returned status no_data (0 matching lines of 1615 read), so it cannot be cited as proof of the absence of application errors; the pod's logs also stop at 09:49:57.85Z, leaving 09:50-09:57 without log data.

load-generator has no traces_span_metrics series in Prometheus (query returned status no_data), so its per-operation error counts are known only from one sampled Jaeger span ('GET', HTTP 504, in trace 40fc89a0cadcbbb31ce5939d98b85f7e).

The query for whether any frontend span exceeded 10s before the incident using a 59m window with a > 0 filter returned status no_data; the equivalent unfiltered comparison over the same 59m window was used instead and showed 0 for all operations.
Node-level CPU, steal or pressure metrics were not queried, so a contribution from node contention cannot be excluded; container-level series for all other otel-demo pods show unchanged throttling.

Whether downstream or customer-visible impact extends beyond the recommendations path is unverified: the only >10s frontend spans are on the recommendations path, but ingress-level request counts for other frontend-proxy routes were not checked.

The sampled span slice a1f471bb-795d-4c1a-a887-d8198c34608f-t0:600a1c2c-92a3-45b3-b893-dd3528ca3bd3 is flagged incomplete and truncated (30 of 340 rows shown), so the 504 list is a sample and not a complete enumeration.
next_steps: Capture a CPU profile and thread/goroutine dump of the recommendation container while it is at its 100m limit and compare with a pre-incident profile to identify what pushed CPU usage from ~0.012 to ~0.10 cores.
Review the recommendation resource settings (request 30m, limit 100m) against real demand and consider raising the limit or enabling autoscaling, then re-measure ListRecommendations latency.
Confirm the frontend-proxy (Envoy) route or upstream timeout from its actual deployment configuration, since the ~15.000s egress expiry sits just under the frontend's ~15.07s response time.
Retrieve the RequestErrorRate rule definition from the alerting layer, since it is absent from this Prometheus, to reconcile the reported 0.0667 value with the observed span-level error ratio.
Check the missing change_history source for any recent deployment, configuration or feature-flag change affecting recommendation or frontend-proxy around 09:40-09:45Z.

Events cover only their own timestamps inside the window; an event that is not returned is unknown, not proof nothing happened (events expire and timestamps are often null). A jq result is what the expression selected, not a full picture of the kind.
